To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the increased oxidizability of VLDLDL in NIDDM subjects is associated with a higher content of unsaturated fatty acids.

1) VLDL from normolipidemia NIDDM patients is more susceptible than controls to oxidation induced by Cu2+ and this increased susceptibility is related to the unsaturated fatty acids content; 2) HDL from normolidemia NIDM patients is more susceptible to oxidation induced by Fe2+ than controls and this increased susceptibility was related to the unsaturate content

VLDL from patients with non-insulin-dependent (Type II) diabetes mellitus are more susceptible to in vitro peroxide-induced oxidation and that this increased susceptibility is related to the content of unsaturated fatty acids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hypothesis of an early involvement of lipoproteins in the pathogenesis and progression of atherosclerosis in diabetes mellitus.
the study of the oxidative stress and the role of the oxidative stress in the development of atherosclerosis.
the possible role of lipoprotein fatty acids in determining the increased susceptibility to oxidation of VLDL of NIDDM patients in good metabolic control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increased susceptibility to peroxidative stress of VLDL, which may be due in part to their fatty acid composition, is a characteristic of the diabetic state and might be related to the increased risk of cardiovascular diseases in diabetic patients.
the increased susceptibility of VLDL to oxidation in NIDDM patients is related with their fatty acid composition.
the susceptibility to oxidation of lipoproteins from patients with diabetes is increased compared to controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fatty acid composition of VLDL is an important determinant of the degree of susceptibility to oxidation in vitro.
NIDDM is a condition of increased susceptibility to peroxidative stress and that this susceptibility is related with the fatty acid composition of lipoproteins.
VLDL and, to a lower extent, HDL are more prone to oxidation in NIDDM than in healthy subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the increased susceptibility to peroxidative stress of VLDL is related with the increased content of unsaturated fatty acids.
VLDL and LDL are more susceptible to oxidation in diabetic patients.
the fatty acid composition of the lipoprotein particles is a key factor in their oxidisability.
